hypothesis: The double expert bank (COLI_CUDA_MOE_DOUBLE=1) also speeds up batched REAP-132 prefill over the single bank, with outputs unchanged, on request 2 (3005 tokens), which each server process serves right after request 1 (the 1992-token prompt of pr1-moe-double-1992.json, counted here as its one warm-up run)
model: DeepSeek V4 Flash REAP 150B (puwaer/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-reap-150b, 132 routed experts, fp4 experts / fp8 dense), colibri safetensors layout, 79 GiB on disk
command: build: cd c && make -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 deepseek-v4 CUDA=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr NVCC=/usr/bin/nvcc CUDA_ARCH=sm_86 NO_TC=1 -j8; run: python3 c/coli serve --model <REAP dir> --ram 40 --ctx 8192 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8090, server environment exactly PATH/HOME/USER/LOGNAME/LANG + the config's env keys (env -i); one freshly started server process per sample (OS page cache not dropped between samples, see notes.cache_state), 3 samples per arm interleaved with the arm order rotated per round (A B C E F / B C E F A / C E F A B); client bench_pr1.py sends request 1 (long_prefill: 1992-token prompt, max_tokens 100) and, for arms A/B/C, then request 2 (long_prefill_2: 3005-token prompt, max_tokens 60), streamed, greedy; tok_s = prompt_tokens / time-to-first-token of the named request; metric: request 'long_prefill_2' (3005 prompt tokens); baseline arm B, trial arm C

hardware.storage: WD_BLACK SN850X 4 TB NVMe (PCIe 4.0), ext4 root filesystem (rw,relatime), model read with O_DIRECT (v4_ssd_io mode=direct-aligned); OS page cache not dropped between samples; round 1 (samples 1-5) partly cold (serve-unit memory peak 7.9G-14.6G vs 7.3G in all 11 later samples), warm from round 2 on
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic, gcc 13.3.0, Python 3.12.3, CUDA toolkit 12.0.140 (generic build CUDA_ARCH=sm_86 NO_TC=1), NVIDIA driver 595.84; 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24 GB, PCIe 4.0 x16-capable cards running at link width x8, NVLink NV4 bridge; only GPU0 used (COLI_GPU=0 DSV4_CUDA_DEVICE=0)

notes.cache_state: The OS page cache was not dropped between samples. Round 1 (samples 1-5: A/s1 B/s1 C/s1 E/s1 F/s1) was partly cold: the serve unit's systemd memory peak (its cgroup, which counts the page cache the unit faulted in) was 13.9G A/s1, 14.6G B/s1, 10.2G C/s1, 9.1G E/s1, 7.9G F/s1, against 7.3G in all 11 later samples (evidence/pr1-host-journal.txt); from round 2 on the page cache was warm. Round 1 holds the lowest request-1 decode rate of every arm and the slowest A request-1 TTFT (A s1 223.9 s vs 218.4/219.1 s). Medians are over all 3 samples; the round-1-excluded ratios (s2/s3 means) are in notes.round1_excluded.
notes.round1_excluded: s2/s3 mean tok/s (round 1 excluded): B 25.1851, C 28.3063, ratio 1.1239
notes.variability: TTFT stdev / CV over 3 samples: B r2 0.081 s / 0.07%; C r2 0.268 s / 0.25%; TTFT coefficient of variation (stdev/mean, 3 samples) is <= 0.32% for every arm and request except A request 1 (1.36%, from the partly cold A s1); TTFT stdev is <= 0.268 s except A request 1 (3.002 s) and A request 2 (0.727 s).
notes.earlier_run_2026_10_14: B median 25.2767 tok/s on 2026-10-14 (48767c01) -> 25.1740 here (-0.41%); C median 28.2847 tok/s on 2026-10-14 (48767c01) -> 28.2551 here (-0.10%); all A/B/C/E/F arm/request medians of this run are -0.41% to -0.06% vs 2026-10-14, all lower; the 1-sample verify arm V, request 1: 12.9944 -> 12.9969 (+0.02%); B..F and V ran an earlier pr1 commit then
notes.outputs: 25 outputs in 16 samples (A 6, B 6, C 6, E 3, F 3, V 1), all byte-identical (full-text sha256) to arm A's per-request reference; 19 of them come from the pr1-tip arms B C E F V.
